cases.sentence: Мне как-то раз случилось прожить две недели в ___ на левом фланге; тут же стоял батальон пехоты; офицеры собирались друг у друга поочередно, по вечерам играли в карты.
cases.explain: «казачьей станице» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: I ONCE happened to spend a couple of weeks in a Cossack village on our left flank. A battalion of infantry was stationed there; and it was the custom of the officers to meet at each other’s quarters in turn and play cards in the evening.

cases.sentence: Рассуждали о том, что ___, будто судьба человека написана на небесах, находит и между нами, христианами, многих поклонников; каждый рассказывал разные необыкновенные случаи pro или contra.
cases.explain: «мусульманское поверье» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: On one occasion--it was at Major S----‘s--finding our game of Boston not sufficiently absorbing, we threw the cards under the table and sat on for a long time, talking. The conversation, for once in a way, was interesting. The subject was the Mussulman tradition that a man’s fate is written in heaven, and we discussed the fact that it was gaining many votaries, even amongst our own countrymen. Each of us related various extraordinary occurrences, pro or contra.

cases.sentence: – Все это, господа, ничего не доказывает, – сказал ___, – ведь никто из вас не был свидетелем тех странных случаев, которыми подтверждаете свои мнения?
cases.explain: «старый майор» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “What you have been saying, gentlemen, proves nothing,” said the old major. “I presume there is not one of you who has actually been a witness of the strange events which you are citing in support of your opinions?”

cases.sentence: – Конечно, никто, – сказали многие, – но мы слышали от ___…
cases.explain: «верных людей» — after the preposition «от», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Not one, of course,” said many of the guests. “But we have heard of them from trustworthy people.”...

cases.sentence: – Все это вздор! – сказал кто-то, – где эти ___, видевшие список, на котором назначен час нашей смерти?..
cases.explain: «верные люди» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “It is all nonsense!” someone said. “Where are the trustworthy people who have seen the Register in which the appointed hour of our death is recorded?... And if predestination really exists, why are free will and reason granted us? Why are we obliged to render an account of our actions?”

cases.sentence: В это время один офицер, сидевший в углу комнаты, встал, и медленно подойдя к столу, окинул всех ___.
cases.explain: «спокойным взглядом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: At that moment an officer who was sitting in a corner of the room stood up, and, coming slowly to the table, surveyed us all with a quiet and solemn glance. He was a native of Servia, as was evident from his name.

cases.sentence: Говорили, однако, что жена полковника была неравнодушна к его ___; но он не шутя сердился, когда об этом намекали.
cases.explain: «выразительным глазам» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: He was brave; talked little, but sharply; confided his thoughts and family secrets to no one; drank hardly a drop of wine; and never dangled after the young Cossack girls, whose charm it is difficult to realise without having seen them. It was said, however, that the colonel’s wife was not indifferent to those expressive eyes of his; but he was seriously angry if any hint on the subject was made.

cases.sentence: Исполнив этот ___, он бросился вперед, увлек за собою солдат и до самого конца дела прехладнокровно перестреливался с чеченцами.
cases.explain: «неприятный долг» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Seven it was!” he cried out, as at length he perceived him in the cordon of skirmishers who were beginning to dislodge the enemy from the wood; and going up to him, he drew out his purse and pocket-book and handed them to the winner, notwithstanding the latter’s objections on the score of the inconvenience of the payment. That unpleasant duty discharged, Vulich dashed forward, carried the soldiers along after him, and, to the very end of the affair, fought the Chechenes with the utmost coolness.

cases.sentence: Когда поручик Вулич подошел к столу, то все замолчали, ожидая от него какой-нибудь ___.
cases.explain: «оригинальной выходки» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: When Lieutenant Vulich came up to the table, we all became silent, expecting to hear, as usual, something original.

cases.sentence: – Держу, – отвечал Вулич ___. – Майор, вы будете судьею; вот пятнадцать червонцев, остальные пять вы мне должны, и сделайте мне дружбу прибавить их к этим.
cases.explain: «глухим голосом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Done,” answered Vulich in a hollow voice. “Major, you will be judge. Here are fifteen ducats, the remaining five you owe me, kindly add them to the others.”
